answer: In a fable contest about an ocean and a glacier, allocate votes by upload capacity, not account count. A fixed verifier gives each stream a fresh random payload and counts its return bytes once before a common deadline, issuing single-use vote credits. One megabyte returned earns one credit; validators reject credits already spent. More keys cannot multiply delivered bytes: another credit requires transmitting another megabyte before the same deadline, consuming uplink capacity. Botnets can aggregate bandwidth, and the verifier is a trusted bottleneck.
